did_you_know.text: The phrase “opener of the womb” means the first offspring to emerge from the womb, not simply the oldest child in a family. In the Torah’s laws, a firstborn human is redeemed, while a firstborn animal is dedicated to God.
“The month of Aviv” refers to the spring month when the barley ripens; in a later period, this month became known as Nisan. The word “Aviv” is also connected with ripe ears of grain.
Chametz is food that has fermented and risen, while se’or is a leavening substance, such as sourdough starter. The verse therefore mentions both the food and the substance that makes it rise.
In Jewish tradition, these verses are among the passages written inside tefillin, worn on the arm and the head. In this way, remembering becomes a daily practice as well as an idea.
“The way of the land of the Philistines” was probably the shorter route along the coast, but it passed through an area where conflict could occur. The shortest route was not always the best one.

The word chamushim is rare and its meaning is uncertain, so translations explain it in different ways: armed, organized, or arranged in groups. It is one of the more difficult words to translate in Exodus.
Joseph had made the Israelites swear that they would carry his bones with them when they left Egypt, and Moses fulfills that oath here. The story thus connects Joseph’s generation with the Exodus.
